Solon Local Knowledge

Solon's Tree Preservation Ordinance

Solon has a tree preservation ordinance with two separate permit categories — residential and commercial. Healthy-tree removal above the city's DBH threshold requires a permit, while hazard trees (dead or dying) follow an expedited process with arborist documentation. Roubic assesses DBH before quoting and handles the permit workflow on your behalf as part of the job.

Commercial removals additionally coordinate with Solon engineering for right-of-way and sidewalk impact. Any actual village permit fee is billed at cost and disclosed upfront — there is no separate Roubic markup.

What Happens If You Defer

The Cost of Waiting — Solon Context

Three scenarios that turn a $700 removal into a $3,000+ emergency job.

EAB Ash Stability Loss

Emerald Ash Borer has killed an estimated 90%+ of NE Ohio's ash. EAB-killed ash turn brittle within 18–24 months and fail violently in storms — many of Solon's remaining dead ash are already at that stage.

Wind-Load Failures

Solon's mature heritage canopy takes hard wind hits every spring. A leaning or dead-crown tree near a house or garage becomes an insurance-deductible event the moment it comes down.

Ordinance & ROW Exposure

Solon's preservation ordinance and commercial right-of-way coordination mean an unaddressed hazard near the ROW can draw village attention. The removal cost stays the same — the delay just adds risk.

Common Solon Removal Questions

Solon Tree Removal FAQ

Six things Solon homeowners and property managers want to know before booking.

How much does tree removal cost in Solon, OH?
Tree removal in Solon typically runs $300–$7,000+ depending on tree size, species, access, and any permit fees. Small trees under 30 ft run $300–$700; medium 30–60 ft trees $700–$1,800; large 60–80 ft heritage oaks $1,800–$3,500; and very-large or crane-required removals $3,500–$7,000+. After-hours emergency dispatch adds roughly a 30% premium. Every estimate is free on-site.
Do I need a permit to remove a tree in Solon?
Solon has a tree preservation ordinance requiring a permit for healthy-tree removal above the city's DBH threshold, with separate residential and commercial categories. Hazard trees (dead or dying) follow an expedited process with arborist documentation. Roubic assesses DBH before quoting and handles the permit workflow for you — only the village's actual permit fee passes through, billed at cost with no markup.
How quickly can Roubic remove a tree in Solon?
Solon is a Tier 1 Roubic service area. Standard removals are typically scheduled within 1–3 business days of estimate sign-off, and active emergencies — tree on a structure, blocking a driveway, or a leaning hazard — get priority next-day or after-hours response from our Auburn Township yard, 7 miles away. Call {{global.phone}} for emergency dispatch.
Will Roubic remove an EAB-killed ash tree in Solon?
Yes. Emerald Ash Borer has killed an estimated 90%+ of ash trees across NE Ohio, including Solon. EAB-killed ash become brittle within 18–24 months and fail violently in storms. We've removed hundreds of EAB-killed ash across the Solon area; the wood is hauled to our Auburn Township firewood yard for seasoning.
What if the tree is near a house, fence, or power line?
Tight-access removals in Solon are routine for our crews. We use sectional dismantling with rigging where bucket-truck access is limited, crane support for heritage trees near structures, and direct coordination with FirstEnergy / The Illuminating Company when work intersects power lines. Insurance documentation is built into every job involving property-protection scenarios.
Is Roubic insured for Solon tree removal jobs?
Yes — Roubic carries general liability and workers-compensation coverage, and a certificate of insurance is available on request. We already have COI on file with several Solon-area HOAs and with the city itself, so repeat and commercial work usually doesn't require a fresh insurance review — often saving 2–3 days off the timeline.
